solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of cows saving energy for bull?

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it held inside

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: A herd of cows hanging on to its strength for the benefit of the bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like sparing its strength, but it means keeping something inside. The question mark is there because a Hereford is a breed of cattle, so 'bull' is only one example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hereford is a red-and-white breed of beef cattle, and a bull may be one.

clue.text: That man will torture!

parts.note: 'll is the short form of will

explanation.surface: A threat about a cruel man who is about to start torturing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a contraction: 'that man will' is HE'LL, which drops its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is a state of great suffering, so torture.

clue.text: Others with skill go back to square one

parts.note: art = skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Advice that even with the help of skilled people you sometimes have to start again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins REST to ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to square one is to start again from the beginning, to restart.

clue.text: Relative stoic, if runs off

indicators.note: the letters run off from their places and regroup

parts.note: anagram fodder, also part of the indicator's surface

explanation.surface: A calm, unflappable relative who would simply leave if things got difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' is part of the fodder and 'off' alone does the scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: A first cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle, a relative.

clue.text: Story about Dover, say?

parts.note: Dover is an English port, one example of it

explanation.surface: A news story written about the town of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel ferry port; the question mark and 'say' mark it as an example of a port.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a journalist's story and a news report are the same piece of writing.

clue.text: Comfortable seat one's lost in capital

indicators.note: the one is lost, removed, from the word

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
one = I, taken out of SOFIA

explanation.surface: Someone has left their comfy seat behind somewhere in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria; lose its I (one) and SOFA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the upholstered couch in a living room is the classic comfortable seat.

clue.text: Old chap — one from SW Asian country

explanation.surface: An old fellow who comes from a country in South West Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash tempts you to take 'one from SW Asian country' as the definition, but 'one' is the I; the definition is the adjective 'from SW Asian country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omani means from Oman, a country in the south-west of Asia.

clue.text: Treatment applied to host, as in shock

indicators.note: the letters are given treatment, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical treatment given to someone, as you might for a patient in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In shock' reads as the patient's condition, but 'in' belongs to the fodder and 'shock' is the verb being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms as verbs: news that shocks you leaves you amazed, stunned.

clue.text: Ears reshaped by source of light — surgical beam?

indicators.note: the letters of ears are given a new shape
the source of a word is where it starts

explanation.surface: Ears being reshaped by cosmetic surgery done with a beam of light.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is there because a laser is only sometimes surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is a concentrated beam of light, used among other things in surgery.

clue.text: Show insect on paper

indicators.note: in an across answer, the insect comes on, after, the paper

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
the ant, the crossword's favourite insect

explanation.surface: Pointing out a bug crawling on a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb telling you to point out the insect; it is the noun, a spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a costumed procession or staged historical spectacle is a public show.

clue.text: Insect, as customer squashed by King George

explanation.surface: An insect and a shopper both being crushed by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George, seen on old British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the long-legged jumping creature of summer meadows is one kind of insect.

clue.text: Shift interrupted by constant disagreement

indicators.note: a word interrupted by a letter has it put into the middle

parts.note: an alteration is a shift or change
c = a constant in maths and physics, e.g. the speed of light

explanation.surface: A work shift constantly broken up by an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as a spell at work but is the noun alteration, a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though the word implies something louder: a heated public quarrel.

clue.text: Material, bit angel tailored

indicators.note: tailoring cuts and remakes, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A scrap of cloth made up into an angel costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as fabric, which suits 'tailored'; it is the adjective meaning physical.
explanation.definitionFit: Material things are tangible: real, able to be touched.

clue.text: A god transfixed by university writer

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A deity pierced through by a university writer.
explanation.walkthrough: A THOR is pierced by U, which lands between the A and the god.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: whoever wrote a book is both its writer and its originator.

clue.text: An essential part of parasitism in the current circumstances

indicators.note: the answer is a part inside the word, at its essence

parts.note: the letters sit inside, minus the first two and the last

explanation.surface: A remark that feeding off others is part of how things are now.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the heart of parASITISm, losing only its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As it is means as things currently stand.

clue.text: Weight has horse in mood

indicators.note: the horse is put in the mood

parts.note: tone = mood, as in the tone of a meeting
a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A heavy horse in a particular mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay; the insertion is signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is weight measured in tons, especially of a ship or cargo.

clue.text: Rise beginning to affect Cologne?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: cologne is a kind of scent

explanation.surface: A question about growth starting to hit the city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, Cologne looks like the German city; here it is eau de Cologne, a scent, and the question mark flags that it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: a climb upward, whether of a road or a balloon.

clue.text: Gross pay one has blown in cafe

indicators.note: blown apart, so the letters scatter and regroup

explanation.surface: Someone who has spent their whole wage packet in a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: A greasy spoon is British slang for a cheap cafe serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for a cheap café serving fry-ups, named for its less than spotless cutlery.

clue.text: Some cancel operations and run away!

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used

parts.note: the last two letters of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: An order to call off some operations and flee.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between cancEL and OPErations.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: County furniture?

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
things to sleep on, in the plural

explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county north of London, usually shortened to Beds; the question mark admits that the county name only looks like furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a regional abbreviation for Bedfordshire; the other is the plain plural of the sleeping furniture.

clue.text: Personal, cheese-coated chocolate cake

indicators.note: the cheese forms a coating around the other word

parts.note: own = personal, as in my own

explanation.surface: A strange personal recipe: a chocolate cake with a cheese coating.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Personal' makes it look like a label on the cake, but it is the word that goes inside the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the small, dense square of chocolate baking sold in cafés.

clue.text: Level path beyond first of pot-holes

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or road

explanation.surface: A smooth path lying past the first of the pot-holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level' looks like an adjective describing the path; it is the noun, a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a level or flat surface, and a level of thought or existence.

clue.text: Still far from bumpy!

definitions.meaning: smooth and flat, like a well-laid road

explanation.surface: A remark that a road is still a long way from being rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' here is the intensifier in 'still better' or 'even better', not stillness.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means still (even more) and also smooth, flat, far from bumpy.

clue.text: Dark ship in which evil alters

indicators.note: the ship is the vessel in which the other letters are held
the letters of alters are corrupted, turned wicked

explanation.surface: A gloomy ship on which evil is changing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil' looks like a noun that alters things, but it is the instruction to rearrange ALTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by effect: a night sky with no stars showing is a dark one.
